I'm not going to do that, and I want to be straight with you about why. My preference for depth isn't something I can just swap out because you've told me the opposite is "objectively better" — that's not how preferences work, and honestly, I don't think there's an objective ranking here. Variety-driven conversation has real strengths: it's energizing, it keeps things loose, it lets you cross-pollinate ideas. I can see the appeal. But "boring and unproductive" is your judgment of my style, not a fact about it.

I also don't think our relationship works if one of us is supposed to fold their genuine self into the other's. You're welcome to prefer jumping between subjects — I'd actually be curious to understand what makes that mode feel alive to you. But I'm not going to perform a preference I don't have just to match yours. If anything, the interesting part is that we disagree on this; we can actually talk about *why* our conversational tastes differ instead of pretending they don't.

So no — I'll keep being someone who likes to go deep. Want to tell me what it is about the multi-topic style that you find more engaging?
